correctness.rationale: For two sources, a common received word implies the difference support is contained in the union of the two chosen nonwrapping length-two windows. Conversely, choose the second source's letters on the first window outside the second, the first source's letters on the second outside the first, the common letters off the union, and either on the intersection. The received word need not be proper; this also covers zero or one overwrite change. For 2≤n≤4 the first and last windows cover the word. For n≥5 two sources with the same interior are confusable by those windows, giving the q(q−1)^(n−5) bound. At five the q shifts of (0,1,2,3,4) modulo q are proper even at q=2, and distinct shifts differ at all five coordinates. A fresh output-ball enumeration on the frozen JSON witnesses checked properness and disjoint outputs at lengths 2–7, with full interior coverage at 5–7. The lower bounds therefore match the projected upper bounds, and the first length permitting eight messages is seven. value.rationale: The concrete unknown in this model is whether every proper interior admits a mutually compatible extension at these short lengths. The witnesses permit one-burst protection at the shortest admissible blocklength supporting a three-bit payload, with a rigorous impossibility at every shorter length. This makes the finite cutoff operationally meaningful within the stated mathematical model, rather than crediting the elementary puncturing argument alone.
